def: Confined to the original tumor site and its nearby tissues and draining lymph nodes, without distant spread. Locoregional recurrence means cancer returning in the same area after treatment.

Divided into small separate pockets (locules) by internal walls, so fluid or pus is walled off. Loculated pleural effusions or abscesses are hard to drain and often need more than simple needle drainage.
Formation of small walled-off compartments within a fluid collection, such as a pleural effusion or abscess, caused by fibrin strands. It traps fluid and makes drainage difficult.
Brand name of clotrimazole, an over-the-counter azole antifungal cream used for athlete's foot, ringworm and yeast infections. Azoles block ergosterol synthesis in the fungal cell membrane.
Poisoning from the bite of a recluse spider (Loxosceles). The venom causes a slowly necrotizing skin ulcer and can trigger hemolysis and kidney injury.
Softening and breakdown of skin or tissue from prolonged wetness. It is seen in skin folds, in diaper rash and between toes, and favors infection.
Urinary albumin excretion above 300 mg per day, a marker of established kidney damage, classically from diabetic nephropathy. It is a higher level than microalbuminuria.
Red blood cells larger than normal (MCV above 100 fL). They appear in vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, alcohol use, liver disease and hypothyroidism.
Skin lesions that combine flat discolored patches (macules) and small raised bumps (papules). Maculopapular rashes are typical of measles, drug reactions and secondary syphilis.
Relating to a malleolus, the bony bump on each side of the ankle (medial malleolus of the tibia, lateral malleolus of the fibula). Malleolar fractures are common ankle injuries.
A fracture that heals in a bad position, producing a deformity or misaligned limb. It differs from nonunion, where the bone fails to heal at all.
A pituitary cell that secretes both growth hormone and prolactin. Tumors from these cells can cause acromegaly together with elevated prolactin.
Pituitary cells that secrete both growth hormone and prolactin. Tumors from these cells can cause acromegaly together with elevated prolactin.
Mannose-rich glycoproteins in the outer layer of the fungal cell wall, such as in Candida and Cryptococcus. They help the fungus adhere to host cells and provoke immune responses.
Surgery that opens a cyst or abscess cavity and stitches its edges to the skin so it drains continuously. It is used for Bartholin gland cysts.
Relating to the upper jaw (maxilla) and lower jaw (mandible) together. Maxillomandibular advancement surgery treats obstructive sleep apnea by moving both jaws forward.
Presence of abnormally large, immature red cell precursors with open nuclei in marrow, caused by impaired DNA synthesis in vitamin B12 or folate deficiency.
Involving both the meninges and the brain's blood vessels. Meningovascular syphilis is an early neurosyphilis form causing inflammation of the arteries and stroke.
A drug that binds acrolein, the toxic bladder metabolite of cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide, preventing hemorrhagic cystitis. Its chemical name is mercaptoethanesulfonate.
The part of the broad ligament of the uterus that lies below the mesosalpinx and mesovarium, attaching to the uterine sides. It is a peritoneal fold supporting the uterus.
Relating to mesothelium, the thin cell layer lining the pleura, pericardium and peritoneum. Mesothelial cells give rise to mesothelioma, which is linked to asbestos.
The thin layer of flat cells lining the pleural, pericardial and peritoneal cavities. Malignant mesothelioma arises from it, classically after asbestos exposure.
The short peritoneal fold of the broad ligament that attaches the ovary to the back of the broad ligament. The ovary is the only pelvic organ not covered by peritoneum.
Describes sequencing all the DNA in a sample at once, without culturing, to identify the organisms present. Metagenomic sequencing can identify unknown pathogens or the gut microbiome.
A norepinephrine analogue labeled with radioactive iodine (MIBG) and taken up by adrenergic tissue. It images pheochromocytoma and neuroblastoma.
An immature granulocyte stage in the marrow, between myelocyte and band cell, with an indented kidney-shaped nucleus. Increased numbers in blood suggest a left shift.
A metabolite of dopamine made by catechol-O-methyltransferase. Elevated levels point to dopamine-secreting pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma.
An organic mercury compound that accumulates in large predatory fish. It crosses the placenta and damages the developing brain, causing neurotoxicity and, in adults, ataxia and paresthesias.
A peripherally acting opioid antagonist that does not cross the blood-brain barrier. It treats opioid-induced constipation without reversing pain relief.
A tiny collection of neutrophils within tissue. Munro microabscesses in the epidermis suggest psoriasis; crypt abscesses of the colon suggest ulcerative colitis.
Pituitary adenomas smaller than 10 mm. They usually cause hormone excess, such as prolactin, rather than mass effects like visual loss.
Needing oxygen, but at lower levels than air (about 5 percent), to grow. Campylobacter and Helicobacter are microaerophilic.
Small amounts of albumin in urine (30-300 mg per day), an early sign of diabetic kidney disease before ordinary dipstick tests turn positive.
Presence of abnormally small red blood cells (MCV below 80 fL), as in iron deficiency, thalassemia and anemia of chronic disease.
Blood in the urine seen only under the microscope, not visibly. It is defined by red cells on urinalysis and prompts evaluation for stones, infection, glomerular disease or cancer.
Causing cells to enter mitosis and divide. Growth factors and some toxins and viral proteins are mitogenic, and excess mitogenic signaling drives cancer.
An enzyme that removes one iodine atom from thyroid hormone. Peripheral deiodinases convert T4 (thyroxine) to active T3 or to inactive reverse T3.
Involving a single synapse between sensory and motor neurons. The stretch (deep tendon) reflex, such as the knee jerk, is monosynaptic.
Enzymes that insert one oxygen atom from O2 into a substrate while reducing the other oxygen to water. Cytochrome P450 enzymes and phenylalanine hydroxylase are examples.
A special stain that colors epithelial mucin red. It highlights the capsule of Cryptococcus neoformans and mucin in adenocarcinomas.
Stagnation of mucus that is not cleared from the airways, as in cystic fibrosis and chronic bronchitis. It promotes infection and airway blockage.
Refers to a multigated acquisition (MUGA) scan, a nuclear imaging test using labeled red cells that measures left ventricular ejection fraction.
A woman who has been pregnant more than once, regardless of the outcomes.
